claims.statement: DEP02-B mean after PM is 517.878 vs 502.323 before, with last PM at 66.97
Post-PM DEP02-B lots LOT-1227 at 517.33 and LOT-1229 at 516.91 and LOT-1231 at 520.0 and LOT-1236 at 517.48 and LOT-1239 at 517.67 stayed high across MET01 and MET02 and CLN01 and CLN02
DEP02-B averaged 513.68 vs 501.9 and 502.82 and 501.62 on other chambers with ANOVA p-value 0.0006, while CLEAN p-value 0.2643 and MET p-value 0.3599 show no upstream or metrology effect
FDC on DEP02-B shows no shift with heater z-score of -0.0 and pressure z-score of -1.1 while recent wafers measured 517.33 and 517.67

disposition.summary: DEP02-B shifted high right after PM at 66.97h and all measured lots since are OOS high on both metrology tools and both clean tools. FDC shows no sensor shift. Hold the alarm lot and hold the chamber for re-qual.

notes.text: Investigating alarm on DEP02-B — pulling the alarm details first.
Alarm wafer reads high at 517.67. I'll trace its history to check for process clues.
Lot traced to CLN01 and DEP02-B at 150 wafers since PM. Checking if other chambers show the same shift.
DEP02-B stands out with high readings while other chambers look normal. I'll run commonality to isolate the source.
Commonality points strongly to DEP02-B. I'll examine its thickness trend for drift or shifts.
Thickness jumped right after the last PM. I'll check the maintenance log to confirm the timing.
PM timing lines up with the shift. I'll check sensor data to rule out a misreport.
Sensors show no shift, so this looks like a real film change. I'll pull recent DEP02-B lots to verify the pattern.
Evidence is decisive for a post-PM chamber shift — both cleans and both metrology tools agree, with no sensor anomaly. Filing the disposition.

truth.explanation: DEP02-B came back from PM at 66.97h running about 18 A thick.

sources.practitioner: Chambers are conditioned and recalibrated after PM, so a shift that survives into production points at the chamber. Engineers check per-tool box plots and time series around the PM.
